concepts.def: A chemical cell contains chemicals which react together to produce electricity. The electricity is not stored inside the cell beforehand: it is produced by the reaction, and only while the reaction can continue and the circuit is complete.

One of the two conducting solids, usually metals, that dip into the electrolyte and are connected into the external circuit. The type of electrode used is one of the factors that determines the voltage a cell produces.
The conducting liquid or paste in which the electrodes are placed. It contains ions that can move, and the type of electrolyte used is one of the factors that determines the voltage a cell produces.

The potential difference produced across the two electrodes of a cell. It depends upon a number of factors, including the type of electrode and the type of electrolyte, not upon how large the cell is.

A cell made by connecting two different metals that are in contact with an electrolyte. The two metals must be different: two identical electrodes react with the electrolyte in the same way and produce no voltage.
Two or more cells connected together in series. Connecting cells in series provides a greater voltage than a single cell, because the voltages of the individual cells add together.
Cells joined end to end so that the same current passes through each one in turn. Joined this way their voltages add, which is why a battery of four 1.5 V cells provides 6.0 V.

A cell in which the chemical reactions cannot be reversed. The reactions stop, and the cell stops producing a voltage, when one of the reactants has been used up. Alkaline batteries are non-rechargeable.
The named example of a non-rechargeable battery in this specification. It cannot be recharged: once one of its reactants has been used up the reactions stop and the battery is replaced.

A cell that can be recharged because the chemical reactions inside it are reversed when an external electrical current is supplied. No new chemicals are added and no waste is removed; the products are turned back into reactants.

In a cell made from two different metals in an electrolyte, the greater the difference in reactivity between the two metals, the greater the voltage produced. This allows voltages for untested pairs to be predicted from reactivity data.

A cell that is supplied by an external source of fuel (eg hydrogen) and oxygen or air. The fuel is oxidised electrochemically within the cell to produce a potential difference, and the cell keeps working for as long as the fuel and oxygen are supplied.

Oxidation carried out at an electrode so that the electrons lost by the fuel travel round the external circuit. This is what allows a fuel cell to produce a potential difference directly, rather than releasing the energy as heat by burning.
The overall reaction is the oxidation of hydrogen to produce water: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O. Water is the only product of the reaction in the cell.

An equation showing what happens at one electrode, including the electrons. In a hydrogen fuel cell with an acidic electrolyte the negative electrode reaction is H2 → 2H+ + 2e− and the positive electrode reaction is O2 + 4H+ + 4e− → 2H2O. Both atoms and charges must balance.

Weighing advantages against disadvantages using evidence: for cells, cost, lifetime, whether they can be recharged and how they are disposed of; for hydrogen fuel cells, the fact that only water is produced set against the difficulty and cost of storing and distributing hydrogen.

mcqs.q: A chemical cell is connected to a lamp and the lamp lights. Where does the electricity come from?
options: From chemicals inside the cell that react together
From electricity stored in the cell already
From a store of electrons in the metal casing
From energy stored inside it, like a battery
mcqs.explain: Cells contain chemicals which react to produce electricity; the reaction runs only once the circuit is complete.

mcqs.q: Two cells are identical except that one uses zinc and copper electrodes and the other uses magnesium and copper. The cells give different voltages. Why?
options: The voltage depends on how much electrolyte there is
The voltage depends on the type of electrode used
The voltage depends on the area of the electrode
The voltage depends on the wire joining them up
mcqs.explain: The voltage produced by a cell depends on a number of factors, including the type of electrode.

mcqs.q: A simple cell uses zinc and copper electrodes in copper sulfate solution. The copper sulfate solution is replaced by a different electrolyte, with everything else unchanged. What happens to the voltage?
options: It stays the same, because only the metals matter here
It stays the same for any liquid, even for pure water
It may change, as the voltage depends on electrolyte
It changes only if the new electrolyte is an acid
mcqs.explain: The voltage produced by a cell depends on the type of electrolyte as well as the type of electrode.

mcqs.q: Which pair of electrodes, dipped into an electrolyte, would produce a voltage?
options: Two identical strips of copper metal
Two copper strips of different size
Two carbon rods taken from cells
A zinc strip and a copper strip
mcqs.explain: A simple cell is made by connecting two different metals in contact with an electrolyte.

mcqs.q: A battery is made by connecting four 1.5 V cells together in series. What voltage does the battery provide, and why?
options: 1.5 V, because the cells share one voltage
6.0 V, because the voltages of the cells add up
6.0 V, because the current from each cell adds
0.375 V, as the voltage is split between them
mcqs.explain: Batteries consist of two or more cells connected in series to provide a greater voltage.

mcqs.q: A non-rechargeable cell stops producing a voltage after some time in use. Why does it stop?
options: All the electrons inside the cell have been used up
The electrolyte has leaked out of its case
One of the reactants has been completely used up
Both of the electrodes have been fully used up
mcqs.explain: In non-rechargeable cells the chemical reactions stop when one of the reactants has been used up.

mcqs.q: Which statement about alkaline batteries is correct?
options: They can be recharged from the mains many times over
They are rechargeable once the alkali is replaced
They work again once fresh reactants are added
They are non-rechargeable, so they are replaced
mcqs.explain: The specification states that alkaline batteries are non-rechargeable.

mcqs.q: A rechargeable cell is connected to an external electrical supply. What happens inside the cell?
options: The chemical reactions are reversed
Fresh reactants are pushed into the cell
Extra electrons are stored inside it
The used-up reactants are all removed
mcqs.explain: Rechargeable cells can be recharged because the chemical reactions are reversed when an external current is supplied.

mcqs.q: Cells are made from a copper electrode and one other metal in the same electrolyte. The voltages are: magnesium 2.7 V, zinc 1.1 V, iron 0.8 V. Tin is less reactive than iron but more reactive than copper. What voltage would a tin and copper cell most likely give?
options: About 1.9 V, from the zinc and iron values added
About 3.4 V, since tin is the least reactive metal
About 0.5 V, because tin is close to copper in reactivity
About 2.7 V, the same as the magnesium cell gives
mcqs.explain: The voltage rises with the difference in reactivity, so tin, just above copper, gives a small voltage.

mcqs.q: Where does the hydrogen in a hydrogen fuel cell come from?
options: It is stored inside the cell when the cell is built
It is made inside the cell from air and water
It is released by the electrolyte as it runs
It is fed in from an external supply of the fuel
mcqs.explain: Fuel cells are supplied by an external source of fuel (eg hydrogen) and oxygen or air.

mcqs.q: In a hydrogen fuel cell, how does the fuel produce a potential difference?
options: It is oxidised electrochemically at an electrode
It is burned, and the heat drives a generator
It is reduced by oxygen at the negative electrode
It is decomposed by a current supplied to the cell
mcqs.explain: The fuel is oxidised electrochemically within the fuel cell to produce a potential difference.

mcqs.q: Which equation represents the overall reaction in a hydrogen fuel cell?
options: H2 + O2 → H2O + O
H2 + O2 → 2H2O
mcqs.explain: The overall reaction is the oxidation of hydrogen to produce water, balanced as 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O.

mcqs.q: Why are hydrogen fuel cells described as a potential alternative to rechargeable cells and batteries?
options: They can be refilled with electricity at any charge point
They store far more electricity inside them than a battery
They need no fuel or oxygen once they have been started
They keep working while hydrogen is supplied, with no recharging
mcqs.explain: A fuel cell runs on an external fuel supply, so it does not have to be taken out of use to recharge.

mcqs.q: A car maker compares a hydrogen fuel cell car with a rechargeable battery car. Which is a genuine disadvantage of the fuel cell car?
options: It gives out carbon dioxide as it is driven
Hydrogen is difficult to store safely
It must be plugged in and recharged often
It stops once its battery has gone flat
mcqs.explain: Hydrogen is a flammable gas that must be stored under pressure or at very low temperature, which is a real drawback.

mcqs.q: (HT) A hydrogen fuel cell has an acidic electrolyte. Which half equation shows the reaction at the negative electrode?
mcqs.explain: Hydrogen is oxidised at the negative electrode, losing electrons: H2 → 2H+ + 2e−.

mcqs.q: (HT) A hydrogen fuel cell has an acidic electrolyte. Which half equation shows the reaction at the positive electrode?
mcqs.explain: Oxygen is reduced at the positive electrode, gaining electrons: O2 + 4H+ + 4e− → 2H2O.

mcqs.q: A games controller is used every day and flattens its cells within a week. Which is the best reason for choosing rechargeable cells for it?
options: They can be reused many times, so fewer cells are bought
Recharging pushes new chemicals in, so they never wear out
They hold much more electricity inside them when new
They cost less to buy than an alkaline cell does
mcqs.explain: With heavy daily use the cost and waste of replacing cells each week outweigh the higher purchase price of a rechargeable cell.
